native_result.query: Between which years did the largest increases in median wealth occur among black females?
native_result.HypoA: The largest increases in median wealth from 1985 to 1990 were among black females, with a percentage increase of 1385.71%.
native_result.HypoB: Interval label: 1985-1990. Among pooled black females (n=1,548; 1,548 respondents observed in each of 1985, 1990 and 1996) median composite wealth rose from $175 in 1985 to $2,600 in 1990 and to $4,000 in 1996, so both candidate intervals are increases and the larger absolute increase occurred between 1985 and 1990 (+$2,425) rather than between 1990 and 1996 (+$1,400), a point difference of $1,025. The supporting percentage changes are +1,385.7% for 1985-1990 and +53.8% for 1990-1996, but the 1985-1990 percentage is not meaningful because the 1985 median of $175 is effectively zero. This conclusion is not robust to how exact-zero wealth values are handled: treating zeros as technical missing (medians $3,832 -> $8,100 -> $19,800; +$4,268 vs +$11,700) or restricting to positive wealth ($4,800 -> $11,057 -> $25,050; +$6,257 vs +$13,993) both reverse the ranking and give 1990-1996 as the interval with the largest increase, on both the absolute and the relative criterion. The 1985-1990 result therefore rests on 39.9% zero-coded 1985 wealth values and on the 1985 median sitting at the edge of a block in which 47.5% of black females are at or below $0; 231 black females report 0 wealth in all three waves, and zero shares roughly double in 1996 for white respondents (20.7/20.3 -> 42.6% and 24.6/25.7 -> 43.3%), which suggests part of the zeros are technical rather than real. A single bootstrap (B=2,000, primary branch) leaves 1985-1990 winning with probability 96.6%, so sampling noise is not what drives the disagreement - the zero-handling rule is. All estimates are unweighted, nominal-dollar point estimates (no weights or variance information exist in the file), no inflation adjustment is applied, rows are assumed to be distinct respondents without deduplication, and the stratification by ever_jailed is not interpretable (n=16).
native_result.WorkflowB: 1) Inspection pass (analysis/inspect_data.py -> analysis/inspection_report.txt): schema, exact label spellings, race x sex counts, missingness, zero/negative mass, confirmation that only composite_wealth_1985/1990/1996 exist (hence exactly two candidate intervals). 2) Filter race=='black' & sex=='female' (lowercase exact match), n=1,548; n identical in all three years, so complete-case vs all-available is moot. 3) PRIMARY branch per ruling (b): zeros kept as real zero wealth, no deduplication; median per year; absolute $ delta per interval as the ranking criterion per ruling (a); % delta as a support column with an explicit flag when the base median is ~0. 4) Two equal-weight sensitivity branches: zeros->NaN and positive-wealth-only, same interval logic. 5) Report BOTH intervals in every branch with medians, $ delta, % delta and sign; explicitly flag that the winning interval changes between branches. 6) Exactly one bootstrap run (B=2,000, seed 20261023, primary branch, resampling the 1,548 respondents) for rank stability, one conclusion. 7) ever_jailed==1 reported as a one-liner (n=16, medians $0/$0/$0, not interpretable). Outputs: analysis/results_report.txt, analysis/results_table.csv, analysis/black_female_distribution_by_year.csv, analysis/hypothesis.md.

sub_hypo.text: The largest increases in median wealth from 1985 to 1990 were among black females, with a percentage increase of 1385.71%.
sub_hypo.context: Participants in the National Longitudinal Study of Youth's 1979 cohort, comparing median wealth from 1985 to 1990 across race and sex groups.
sub_hypo.relations: Black females had the largest percentage increase in median wealth from 1985 to 1990 among race and sex groups, at 1385.71%.

gold_sub_hypo.full_hypo: The largest increases in median wealth from 1985 to 1990 were among black females, with a percentage increase of 1385.71%.

sub_hypo.text: When exact-zero wealth is retained, pooled black females have rising median composite wealth in both candidate intervals, with the larger absolute increase in 1985–1990.
sub_hypo.context: National Longitudinal Study of Youth 1979 cohort; race=='black' and sex=='female', 1,548 respondents observed in each of 1985, 1990 and 1996. Estimates are unweighted nominal dollars without inflation adjustment; rows are assumed distinct without deduplication. Zeros are retained as real wealth, and intervals are ranked by absolute median-dollar change.
sub_hypo.relations: Median wealth rises from $175 to $2,600 to $4,000. The 1985–1990 increase of $2,425 exceeds the 1990–1996 increase of $1,400 by $1,025. Supporting percentage increases are 1,385.7% and 53.8%, respectively, but the former is not meaningful because the $175 baseline is effectively zero.

sub_hypo.text: The interval ranking reverses when zeros are treated as technical missing values or wealth is restricted to positive values.
sub_hypo.context: Same pooled black-female cohort and unweighted, nominal-dollar, non-deduplicated analysis; two equal-weight sensitivity branches use zeros-to-missing and positive-wealth-only rules.
sub_hypo.relations: With zeros treated as missing, medians are $3,832, $8,100 and $19,800, giving increases of $4,268 and $11,700. With positive wealth only, medians are $4,800, $11,057 and $25,050, giving increases of $6,257 and $13,993. Both rules rank 1990–1996 above 1985–1990 by both absolute and relative increase, reversing the primary result.

sub_hypo.text: The primary 1985–1990 ranking depends on the concentration of zero-coded wealth, and observed zero patterns suggest some zeros may be technical rather than real.
sub_hypo.context: Distributional checks in the NLSY1979 dataset, primarily among the 1,548 black females, with supporting zero-share comparisons for white respondents.
sub_hypo.relations: Among black females, 39.9% have zero-coded 1985 wealth and 47.5% have wealth at or below $0, placing the $175 median at the edge of that block; 231 report zero wealth in all three waves. White respondents' zero shares roughly double in 1996: 20.7%/20.3% to 42.6% and 24.6%/25.7% to 43.3%. These patterns suggest, rather than establish, that some zeros are technical.

sub_hypo.text: The primary interval ranking is stable under respondent bootstrap resampling, indicating that zero handling rather than sampling noise drives the disagreement between branches.
sub_hypo.context: Black females, n=1,548; primary branch retaining zeros; exactly one bootstrap with 2,000 respondent resamples and seed 20261023. No weights or variance information exist in the file.
sub_hypo.relations: The 1985–1990 interval has the larger absolute increase in median wealth in 96.6% of bootstrap resamples, despite its ranking reversing under alternative zero-handling rules.

sub_hypo.text: The ever-jailed black-female subgroup has zero median wealth in all three waves, but its stratified results are not interpretable.
sub_hypo.context: Black females with ever_jailed==1, indicating incarceration between 1985 and 1994; n=16.
sub_hypo.relations: Median composite wealth is $0 in 1985, 1990 and 1996; the subgroup size of 16 makes the incarceration stratification uninterpretable.

Malformed judge output raises an evaluation error; no hidden retries.
evaluator_config.aggregation: recall_context * mean_accuracy_score; unmatched predicted contexts stay in denominator
evaluator_config.native_behavior_preserved: Variable/relation comparisons receive full hypotheses for each matched context pair.

details.score_scope: Reference agreement of submitted hypothesis; execution is not independently verified by this native metric.
